result.instructions:
opentide: Spec-driven development for agentic detection engineering. opentide gives every detection an ontology and a taxonomy, so it stays threat-aligned, maintainable and fast to ship, with or without agents.

The catalogue is YAML in the repository: threats (objects/threats/), objectives (objects/objectives/) and rules (objects/rules/). A rule's detection_model is an objective UUID; an objective lists threat UUIDs.

Workflow:
1. Search. search (keyword, UUID, technique) and coverage find what exists; get_chaining shows threat -> objective -> rule.
2. Draft. Start from opentide://templates/{object_type}, check fields against opentide://schemas/{object_type} and opentide://vocabularies/{name}, and write the file with your own tools: this server does not write files.
3. Validate until clean. Call validation_report with file or uuid after every edit. Each issue has code, severity, message, object_uuid, path, line and column (1-based), help, and fix ({safe, edits}: each edit replaces the text from (line, column) up to (end_line, end_column) with replacement). Apply safe edits as they are: they only respell the same word; check the others against help. explain(code) says what a code means. Repeat until ok is true. While drafting a query, validate_query checks it offline in its platform's language, with no tenant.
4. Preview. deploy_rule with dry_run true shows the deployment; nothing is sent.

People review and merge changes and run real deployments. Call deploy_rule with dry_run false only when a person asks for it. validate_query with live true contacts the tenant with the configured credentials: ask first. run_query with live true runs a read-only query on a tenant and returns its rows: ask first as well.

Results may carry next_actions: [{tool, arguments, command, reason}], the next call to make (command is the same step as an opentide command line). Read the reason before following one.

tools.description:
Find threats, objectives and rules. Start here when you have no UUID.

query: a UUID (exact, case-insensitive) or text matched against uuid, title,
name and description; "" matches everything the filters allow.
Filters: type (rule | threat | objective), platform (exact configuration key:
sentinel never matches sentinel_one), status (a rule platform block status, exact), technique
(ATT&CK id, case-insensitive), actor (att&ck::G0006 or G0006).
Returns a list of {uuid, type, title, status}; [] when nothing matches.
Read opentide://rules/{uuid} (threats/, objectives/) for the full object.
tools.name: search

tools.description:
Threat -> objective -> rule lineage of any object, before you edit or add one.

Returns {uuid, found, type, graph, lineage: {threats, objectives, rules},
chaining_index}. graph is the lineage, or {relation: [threat uuids]} for a
threat with threat.chaining entries. An unknown UUID returns only {uuid,
found: false, graph: {}}.
tools.name: get_chaining

tools.description:
ATT&CK coverage: which rules detect a technique, and where the gaps are.

technique (T1059): {technique, covered, matched_techniques, rules}; a parent
technique also matches its sub-techniques. Empty: {technique_count, matrix:
{technique: [rule uuids]}, tactic_filter}. tactic is echoed, never filtered on.
tools.name: coverage

tools.description:
Validate one rule by UUID: schema, vocabularies and references.

Returns {valid, errors, warnings, issues, next_actions}. errors and warnings
are strings; issues are structured like validation_report's. Prefer
validation_report, which also takes a file path and returns warnings as
structured entries.
tools.name: validate_rule

tools.description:
Validate objects and return every issue with its position and fix. Call after each edit.

Narrow with file (repository-relative or absolute path; a bare file name
matches every object file of that name), uuid, or object_type (rule |
threat | objective). No argument validates the whole catalogue. Every
rule query is checked offline: queries is error (a query the platform
would reject is an issue), warn (a warning) or off (not checked).
Returns {ok, issues, warnings, stats, next_actions}. Each issue: code,
severity, message, object_uuid, field_path, path, line, column, end_column
(1-based Unicode code points; end_column exclusive), help, fix ({safe,
edits: [{line, column, end_line, end_column, replacement}]} or null),
explain. safe edits only respell the same word; check the others against
help. yaml_line is 0-based and file_path absolute, kept for older clients.
Done when ok is true.
tools.name: validation_report

tools.description:
What a diagnostic code means, an example, and how to fix it.

code: an issue's code, such as vocab_unknown. Returns {found, code, meaning,
markdown}. An unknown code returns found false and the closest code as
suggestion. Empty: {found, codes: [{code, meaning}]}, every code.
tools.name: explain

tools.description:
Check one query offline with the analysis engine, or the catalogue's rules on the tenant.

live false (default) parses query in its platform's language, with the
platform's profile (Defender tables for defender_for_endpoint, Carbon Black
Lucene for carbon_black_cloud, the correlation-rule checks for crowdstrike's
CQL), and returns {valid, status, language, errors, warnings, diagnostics};
positions are in the query (1-based, code points). Elastic takes language:
esql, eql, kuery (default) or lucene, and stack (such as "9.5") for ES|QL.
Offline: carbon_black_cloud, crowdstrike, defender_for_endpoint, elastic, sentinel, splunk, sysdig.
live true contacts the tenant with the configured credentials and validates
the catalogue rules for platform, not query; ask a person first.
Platforms: carbon_black_cloud, defender_for_endpoint, elastic, sentinel, sentinel_one, splunk; others return
supported false.
tools.name: validate_query

tools.description:
Run a read-only query on a platform's tenants and return the rows (live true only).

live false refuses without contacting a tenant. live true sends query, or
the query of the rule whose UUID is rule, to the tenant named by tenant
(comma-separated names, "all", or empty for the only one) over the last
since (15m, 24h, 7d) and returns {status, results: [{tenant, status,
columns, rows, row_count, truncated, warnings, error}], row_count}, at
most limit rows per tenant. It uses the configured credentials: ask a
person first. language is Elastic's: esql, eql, lucene or kuery. index
names Elastic index patterns (comma-separated) or a CrowdStrike repository.
tools.name: run_query

tools.description:
Preview one rule's deployment to a platform. dry_run false deploys it for real.

Returns {action: dry-run | deploy | error, rule_id, status, dry_run, platform,
message}. When nothing was deployed, action is error and status is failed,
not_found or unknown_platform. Keep dry_run true unless a person asks for a
real deployment: people review, merge and deploy.
tools.name: deploy_rule

tools.description:
Where a rule is deployed: vendor ids and tenants per platform.

Returns {uuid, found, platforms: {name: {deployed, rule_id, external_ids,
tenants}}}; state_error when the rule's deployment state cannot be read.
tools.name: deployment_status
